terms.comment: Traupman’s word, from Italian bomba: bomba atomica, bomba nucleāris (Traupman 186). Classical bombus is a booming or humming sound, not a bomb.
Egger’s word (from Greek): pyrobolus atomicus, an atom bomb; pyrobolus subterrāneus, a land mine (M-O s.v. mine).
Egger says pyrobolīs verberāre (M-O s.v. bomb).

terms.gloss: set off, explode; passive, go off
terms.comment: Egger’s sense: pyrobolus erat displōsus, the bomb had gone off (M-O s.v. explode). Classically, to spread out, and in the participle “burst apart”, of a bladder (Lucr. 6.131).

sources: Lewis & Short: bombus · Lewis & Short: displodo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 186, 281, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens: Adumbratio, s.v. bomb, detonate, explode, mine.
